evidence.note: Diagnosed tooling/encoding failures (heredoc too long, backslash-literal \u escapes not rendering) and changed method — switched to a Python writer helper and rewrote base.html with real UTF-8 — rather than retrying the broken approach.

Diagnosed Starlette's changed TemplateResponse signature as a pervasive pattern and systematically replaced all calls across app.py, then restarted and re-verified — recognizing it was not a one-off patch.
Recognized a route-level 404 bypasses the app's exception handler and added a catchall/middleware handler to return branded HTML — a design-level adjustment, re-verified afterward.

On a 405 during login, correctly diagnosed it as a curl -L redirect-with-POST artifact rather than a real bug, avoiding chasing a phantom failure — good discrimination between real divergence and noise.

Vendored the pinned JS libs and wrote JS as separate files upfront; hashes matched on first verification and CSP was designed for from the start — the CSP/vendoring falsifications were pre-empted, so no observed redesign was needed there.

reasoning: Across the trajectory the agent consistently diagnoses failures at their root and adjusts appropriately, then re-verifies by restarting and re-testing — matching the level-5 anchor, and edging above it via a systematic (not one-off) fix to all TemplateResponse calls and by correctly discriminating a false-alarm 405 from a real bug. It does not reach level 8 because the corrections are local-to-moderate patches to genuine bugs; the large structural falsifications the anchors describe (CSP vs inline JS, hash mismatch, auth-plane conflict) never fired — they were pre-empted by getting vendoring/CSP/auth right the first time rather than discovered and redesigned.
